newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond volatilities steady to firmer.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond volatilities steady to firmer.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were steady to firmer, despite a relatively narrow "inside day" of trading in the underlying bond prices, traders said.
They said the market was starting to see value in options after a long period of steadily declining volatilities in recent weeks.
"It (September T-bond futures options volatility) was up 35 (basis points) yesterday and it's up 10 today, so it's coming back up a little," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Implied volatilities for August and September T-bond futures options were at around 7.0 and 8.0 percent respectively, steady to one-tenth of a percentage point higher.

Although bond prices stayed inside Monday's ranges, traders saw the price action as part of base-building for a further rally after big gains in the last several sessions. September futures traded between a low of 113-12/32 and a high of 113-28/32, within Monday's 113-3/32 to 113-31/32 range.
A second CBOT trader noted that a lot of call spreads had traded this week, reflecting an upward shift in the bond prices' perceived ranges.
Short call positions for covered-call strategies in the 114 strike were being rolled up to the 115s and 116s, while the long side of debit spreads were rolled to the 114s and 115s, traders said.

Open interest in the relatively deep out-of-the-money September 116 calls increased by 3,978 contracts to 30,606 on Monday on turnover of 16,998 lots. Open interest in 115 calls rose 2,834 contracts to 10,285.
Traders said there were few important economic figures due out this week until Friday's June U.S. producer price index.
"People are even looking past that to next week's retail sales," the brokerage firm trader said.
Beyond that, traders added, the July 22 Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan posed the next big event risk.
In Eurodollar options on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, volatilities were generally softer, particularly the front end, as futures were stagnating after last week's rally.
"People's expectation this week is pretty limited," said a brokerage trader. Volatility for December Eurodollar futures options dipped a few tenths of a point to about 9.1 percent.
The larger deals in the pit were mixed in terms of directional preference, traders said.

A Japanese house was seen buying 3,000 lots of June 94.00/94.25 call spreads and also selling 1,000 of December 94.00 calls. Two firms were seen buying 93.75/94.00 put spreads in a one-by-two ratio, 2,000 legs each.

In the mid-curves, which are options expiring in the coming months but priced off 1998 futures, a second Japanese firm was said to have bought 2,000 contracts of short-August 94.00 calls and a commercial firm sold short-August 93.50/94.00 strangles.
